name: CHOR VOLI
description: Chor Voli is a traditional Afghan partition card game where players divide their 13-card hands into up to four 3-card combinations, similar to Brag hands. These combinations are then played out in a series of showdowns starting with each player's strongest hand. The game is related to the British game Crash and the Pakistani variant Ramchi.

These combinations are then played out in a series of showdowns starting with each player's strongest hand. The game is related to the British game Crash and the Pakistani variant Ramchi.

Country/Region of Origin: Afghanistan
Time Period: 20th century
Historical Development: Learned by Gyula Zsigri from Sherzod Lukmoni in 1992. A similar game called Ramchi was described in 2011 by Tilman Schieber, said to have come from Pakistan where it is popular with Afghan refugees.
Cultural Significance: Played in Afghanistan and by Afghan refugee communities in Pakistan.

Minimum Players: 4
Maximum Players: 4
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: No, individual play

Type: Standard 52-card international pack
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included

Standard 52-card deck
Chips or counters for scoring
Table space

Cards per Player: 13 cards each
Dealing Pattern: Counterclockwise
Dealer: Left-hand opponent cuts, dealer can deal in any convenient packets
